(Commit as many sins as you can, for you will reach a forgiving Lord; you will bite your palms in regret for the joy you abandoned for fear of the Fire.)
And among that is his saying:
يا كبير الذنب عفو الله من ذنبك أكبر
(O you of great sin, Allah's pardon is greater than your sin.)
However, he repented in the last part of his life, and we may discern the sincerity of his repentance from his poems composed at that age close to the end. He said, acknowledging that he had delayed it until its time had passed:
دبّ فيّ الفناء سفلا وعلوا ... وأراني أموت عضوا فعضوا ذهبت شرّتي وجدة نفسي ... وتذكرت طاعة الله
نضوا ليس من ساعة مضت بي إلا ... نقصتني بمرها لي
جزوا لهف نفسي على ليال وأيا ... م سلكتهن لعبا
ولهوا قد أسأنا كل الإساءة يا ... رب فصفحا عنا إلهي وعفوا
(Decay has crept into me, below and above, and I see myself dying limb by limb. My fervour and my soul's vigour are gone, and I have remembered obedience to Allah, worn out. No hour passes me but by its passing it diminishes a part of me. Alas for the nights and days I spent in play and amusement! We have done every wrong, O Lord, so forgive us, my God, and pardon.)

dervis-irab:7-14.t:
* Vocabulary:
(آنَسْتُ): I perceived from afar. One says «آنست نارا» (I perceived a fire), «آنست فزعا» (I perceived alarm) and «آنست منه رشدا» (I perceived soundness of judgment in him); so it is used of the material and the abstract.
(بِشِهابٍ قَبَسٍ): it is read with annexation and without it, as will come in the I'rab. «الشهاب» is anything luminous generated from fire; also what is seen like a star that has darted down; also a star in general; also a spearhead, because of its glitter. Its plurals are «شهب», «شهبان», «شهبان» [Translator's note: so in the source, the same form printed twice; presumably shuhbān and shihbān] and «أشهب». One says "So-and-so is a shihāb of war" when he is keen in it. «القبس», with two fatḥas, is fire taken as a brand; you say: «خذ لي قبسا من النار» (take a brand of the fire for me), and «مقبسا» and «مقباسا»; «اقبس لي نارا» and «اقتبس». From it: "You are only like the hasty fire-taker (al-qābis al-ʿajlān)", i.e., the one taking a brand; "My visiting you is only like the hasty taking of a brand"; and you say: "I am only a brand from your fire and a handful from your traces." «قبسته نارا» and «أقبسته» (I gave him fire), as you say «بغيته الشيء» and «أبغيته». Figuratively: «قبسته علما وخبرا» (I gave him knowledge and news), and «أقبست».
(تَصْطَلُونَ): it contains substitution (ibdāl), because its original is «تصتلون»; when the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl form came after a letter of covering (iṭbāq), namely the ṣād, it was changed to ṭāʾ according to the rule. It is from «صلي بالنار», with kasra on the lām. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «صلي بالنار and صليها, ṣalan, of the pattern of taʿiba: he felt its heat. Al-ṣilāʾ, on the pattern of kitāb, is the heat of the fire. صليت اللحم أصليه, of the pattern of ramā: I roasted it.» In al-Asās: «صلي النار and صلي بها; "يصلى النار الكبرى"; تصلّاها, تصلّى بها, أصلاه and صلّاه; and a شاة مصليّة is a roasted sheep, and I have roasted it.»
(جَانٌّ): a snake of light, quick movement. In al-Qāmūs and al-Tāj it says: «al-jānn is a collective noun for the jinn; also a snake with dark-rimmed eyes that does no harm, common in houses.» They said it is very large, even though it is light in speed of movement.
(وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ): and did not come back. One says «عقب المقاتل» when the fighter turns back to attack after fleeing. The poet said:
فما عقبوا إذ قيل هل من معقب ... ولا نزلوا يوم الكريهة منزلا
(They did not turn back when it was asked, "Is there anyone to turn back?", nor did they take a stand on the day of battle.)
He describes a people as cowardly: if it was said, "Is there anyone who will turn back on his heels to the fight?", they did not return to it, nor did they take any position in it on the day of war. In al-Mukhtār: «You say: he turned his back in flight and did not «يعقب», with doubled and kasra-vowelled qāf, i.e., he did not turn round and did not wait.»
(جَيْبِكَ): the collar-opening of your shirt; it is called «جيب» because it is «يجاب», i.e., cut, so that the head may enter it.
(وَاسْتَيْقَنَتْها): istīqān is more intensive than īqān, so there is no sense in the saying of some exegetes that the sīn is merely additional.

* I'rab:
(إِذْ قالَ مُوسى لِأَهْلِهِ: إِنِّي آنَسْتُ ناراً): resumptive speech, brought to relate five of the stories of the ancients: the first is the story of Moses, followed by the story of the ants, then the story of Bilqīs, then the story of Ṣāliḥ, then the story of Lot. The adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember"; its determination has been given many times. The clause «قال» is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; «موسى» is the fāʿil (agent) and «لأهله» are attached to «قال». The clause «إني آنست نارا» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); «إن» and its noun, the clause «آنست» its khabar (predicate), and «نارا» the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). «أهله» refers to his wife, the daughter of Shuʿayb, his child and his servant; that was on his return [Translator's note: the source prints «فقوله», evidently for «قفوله»] from Midian to Egypt to meet his mother and brother in Egypt. It has also been said that no one was with him but his wife, and Allah referred to her by «الأهل», and accordingly the address was given in the plural.
(سَآتِيكُمْ مِنْها بِخَبَرٍ أَوْ آتِيكُمْ بِشِهابٍ قَبَسٍ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلُونَ): the clause is resumptive. «آتيكم» is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anā" (I), and the kāf is the direct object. He used the sīn of deferment to indicate that he would return even if he were slow, for perhaps the distance was far. «منها» are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an adjective of «خبر»; «بخبر» are attached to «آتيكم». «أو» is a conjunction; there is a secret in turning from the wāw to «أو», which will come in the Rhetoric section. «آتيكم» is conjoined to the first «آتيكم»; «بشهاب» are attached to «آتيكم»; «قبس» is a badal (substitute) of «شهاب», or a naʿt (adjective) of it on interpreting it as a passive, i.e., a flame taken from a fire. It was also read with annexation, because a shihāb may be a brand (qabas) or something else, like a star; so it is the annexation of the species to its genus, like «خاتم فضة» (a ring of silver) and «ثوب خز» (a garment of silk), and it carries the sense of «من». «لعلكم تصطلون»: the clause of hope is a ḥāl; «لعل», its noun and its khabar; i.e., hoping to secure and provide warmth for you.
(فَلَمَّا جاءَها نُودِيَ أَنْ بُورِكَ مَنْ فِي النَّارِ وَمَنْ حَوْلَها): the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted for brevity. «لما» is a temporal adverb meaning "when" (ḥīniyya), or a linking particle. «جاءها» is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object. The clause «نودي» has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of «نودي» is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he), referring to Moses. «أن» is the explicative (mufassira) one, because calling contains the meaning of saying without its letters, and the meaning is "it was said to him: blessed is…". It may also be in its normal function, i.e., making the imperfect verb accusative, here entering on a past verb; or lightened from the heavy (inna); and «أن» with what follows it is, as an interpreted maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e., «بأن بورك». There are other parsings which we have passed over because they are weak. «بورك» is a passive past verb, and «من» the deputy agent; «في النار» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of «من», i.e., in the place of the fire. «ومن حولها» is conjoined to «من في النار». What is meant by «من» is either Allah the Exalted, with an omission, i.e., His power and authority; or, it has been said, Moses; or, it has been said, «من» refers to non-rational things, namely the light and the places around it.
(وَسُبْحانَ اللَّهِ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; «سبحان» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb; «الله» is muḍāf ilayhi; «رب العالمين» is a badal or an adjective.
(يا مُوسى إِنَّهُ أَنَا اللَّهُ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ): «يا» is a vocative particle and «موسى» is the one addressed (munādā), a single proper name. «إن» and its noun; the hāʾ is either the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) or refers to what the preceding indicates, i.e., "the one speaking to you". «أنا» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «الله» its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of «إن»; «العزيز الحكيم» are two adjectives.
(وَأَلْقِ عَصاكَ فَلَمَّا رَآها تَهْتَزُّ كَأَنَّها جَانٌّ وَلَّى مُدْبِراً وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ): the wāw is a conjunction; «ألق» is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter, and its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "anta" (you). The speech is conjoined to «بورك», because the meaning is "he was called: that blessed is the one in the fire, and that: throw your staff", and this is what makes it preferable that «أن» is explicative, as stated. «عصاك» is the object. «فلما»: the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted, i.e., "so he threw it and it turned into a snake; and when…". «لما» is an adverb meaning "when", or a linking particle; the clause «رآها» is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; «رآها» is a verb, its agent and its direct object. The clause «تهتز» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, because the seeing here is visual. «كأنها جان»: «كأن», its noun and its khabar, and the clause is in the position of accusative as a second ḥāl; or it is a ḥāl of the pronoun of «تهتز», making it an overlapping (mutadākhila) ḥāl. The clause «ولى» has no grammatical position, and «مدبرا» is a ḥāl of the agent of «ولى». The wāw is a conjunction; «لم» is a particle of negation, inversion and jussive, and «يعقب» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by «لم».
(يا مُوسى لا تَخَفْ إِنِّي لا يَخافُ لَدَيَّ الْمُرْسَلُونَ): the clause is the object of an omitted saying which must be implied, i.e., the Exalted said. «يا موسى»: one addressed, a single proper name. «لا» is the prohibitive lā and «تخف» an imperfect verb, jussive by «لا». «إن» and its noun, and the clause «لا يخاف» its khabar; the clause gives the reason for the prohibition of fear. «لدي» is an adverb attached to «يخاف», and «المرسلون» is the agent.
(إِلَّا مَنْ ظَلَمَ ثُمَّ بَدَّلَ حُسْناً بَعْدَ سُوءٍ): «إلا» is a particle of exception meaning "but" (lākin), because the exception is disjoined (munqaṭiʿ); «من» is a relative noun, excepted, in the position of accusative. It may also be conditional, in which case it is a mubtadaʾ and the clause is excepted from the most general of states. «ظلم» is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); «ثم بدل» is conjoined to «ظلم»; «حسنا» is the direct object, and «بعد سوء» is an adverb attached to an omitted adjective of «حسنا».
(فَإِنِّي غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): the fāʾ falls in the reply to «من» on both views; «إن», its noun and its two khabars.
(وَأَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فِي جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضاءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوءٍ): the wāw is a conjunction, and «أدخل» is conjoined to «وألق عصاك»; «يدك» is the direct object and «في جيبك» are attached to «أدخل». «تخرج» is an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the reply to the command; the agent of «تخرج» is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "hiya" (it). «بيضاء» is a ḥāl of the agent of «تخرج», and «من غير سوء» are attached to «بيضاء» because of the verbal meaning in it; this has preceded in Ṭāhā. Abū al-Baqāʾ preferred that the preposition and its genitive noun be another ḥāl, and al-Samīn preferred that it be an adjective of «بيضاء».
(فِي تِسْعِ آياتٍ إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ وَقَوْمِهِ إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا قَوْماً فاسِقِينَ): resumptive speech. The preposition is attached to the omitted verb, i.e., "go with nine signs to Pharaoh". Some determined it as an omitted word, i.e., "sent", so that its position is accusative as a ḥāl; the first is preferable, and it has parallels. The poet said:
فقلت إلى الطعام فقال منهم ... فريق يحسد الإنس الطعاما
(I said: "[Come] to the food!" and a party of them said: "We envy humans their food.")
There are many divergent views of the grammarians which we will give in the Benefits section to sharpen the mind.
«قومه» is conjoined to «فرعون». The clause «إنهم» gives the reason for the command to go; the clause «كانوا» is the khabar of «إن»; «قوما» is the khabar of «كانوا» and «فاسقين» an adjective. The nine signs have been discussed before.
(فَلَمَّا جاءَتْهُمْ آياتُنا مُبْصِرَةً قالُوا هذا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ): the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted, as stated many times. «مبصرة» is a ḥāl, and its meaning will come in the Rhetoric section. The clause «قالوا» has no grammatical position. «هذا» is a mubtadaʾ, «سحر» its khabar and «مبين» an adjective, and the clause is the object of the saying.
(وَجَحَدُوا بِها وَاسْتَيْقَنَتْها أَنْفُسُهُمْ ظُلْماً وَعُلُوًّا): «جحدوا» is conjoined to «قالوا»; «بها» are attached to «جحدوا». The wāw is of ḥāl, with «قد» implied after it. «استيقنتها أنفسهم» is a past verb, a fronted direct object and a postponed agent. «ظلما» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), because it is the cause of the denial, or a ḥāl of the agent of «جحدوا», i.e., wrongdoing and arrogant.
(فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الْمُفْسِدِينَ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (of the implied condition). «انظر» is an imperative verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "anta". «كيف» is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as the fronted khabar of «كان», and «عاقبة المفسدين» is the noun of «كان». The clause suspends «انظر» [Translator's note: the source prints «لا نظر», evidently for «لانظر»] from governing, so it is in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition, because «انظر» means "reflect".

* Rhetoric:
1- Using «أو» instead of the wāw:
In His words «آنست نارا سآتيكم منها بخبر أو آتيكم بشهاب قبس لعلكم تصطلون», He preferred «أو» to the wāw for a wonderful rhetorical point: «أو» conveys choice (takhyīr), and he built his hope on the idea that, if he did not obtain both his needs together, he would not lack one of them — either guidance on the road or taking a brand of fire — out of humility and acknowledgement of his shortcoming before his Lord. The night was wintry and dark, he had lost the road, and his wife had been seized by labour pains. This is a place where the pens of writers who do not grasp the secrets of eloquence slip, especially in the use of conjunctions and prepositions; this art has been pointed out before.
2- Majāz ʿaqlī (rational metaphor):
In attributing seeing to the signs in His words «فلما جاءتهم آياتنا مبصرة». It may also be a majāz mursal (synecdochic metaphor) whose relationship is causality, because they are the cause of seeing. This is better than the saying of some that «مبصرة» is an active participle by which the passive participle is meant — the active participle being applied to the passive to signal that, because of their extreme clarity and illumination, it is as if they would see themselves, were they among things that see.

* Benefits:
The views of the grammarians on «في تسع آيات»:
The views of the grammarians have diverged on the i'rab of this verse, «في تسع آيات إلى فرعون وقومه». In the I'rab we have chosen for you the best and easiest of them, and we will give the remaining views, since they are reported and reasonable, so that they sharpen your mind and you may choose from them what you see as nearest to logic; for i'rab is logic before anything else.
As for al-Zamakhsharī, he confined himself to the view we chose in the I'rab. He said: «"في تسع آيات" is resumptive speech, and the preposition in it is attached to something omitted; the meaning is "go with nine signs", i.e., among the total of nine signs and their number. Someone may say: the signs were eleven, two of them the hand and the staff, and the nine are: the splitting [of the sea], the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the obliteration, drought in their deserts and decrease in their crops.»
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «في تسع» is a third ḥāl — by the first and second ḥāls he meant His word «بيضاء» and His words «من غير سوء» — and «إلى فرعون» is attached to something omitted, its implied form being "sent to Pharaoh"; it may also be an adjective of «تسع» or of «آيات», i.e., reaching Pharaoh.
Al-Zajjāj made «في» mean «من» and attached it to «ألق». He said: as you say «خد لي من الإبل عشرا فيها فحلان» [Translator's note: «خد» is as printed; «خذ» (take) is intended] — "take for me ten camels among which are two stallions", i.e., of them two stallions.
As for Ibn ʿAṭiyya, he supported al-Zajjāj in attaching it to «ألق» and made «في» mean «مع» (with), because the hand and the staff are then included in the nine signs. He said: its implied sense is "that is prepared for you and spread among nine". Others said it is as Ibn ʿAṭiyya said, but the hand and the staff are outside the nine.
Al-Jalāl [al-Maḥallī] chose that it be attached to an omitted word that is another ḥāl of the pronoun of «تخرج»; this omitted word is stated explicitly in Sūrat Ṭāhā, where He says: «تخرج بيضاء من غير سوء آية أخرى». So the meaning here is: being a sign included among the total of the nine signs.

dervis-irab:65-70.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ لا يَعْلَمُ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ الْغَيْبَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَما يَشْعُرُونَ أَيَّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ): this verse has occupied the exegetes, the parsers and the grammarians, and they have gone into it at length. We will choose here the easiest of their views, and will cite in the Benefits section everything that has been said about it, because of the enjoyable mental exercise in that. The clause is resumptive, introduced to answer them, since they had asked him about the time of the coming of the Hour. (لا) is negative and (يعلم) is an imperfect verb; (من) is a relative noun, the fāʿil (agent) of (يعلم); (في السموات والأرض) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (من), i.e. "the one who is fixed, settled and dwelling in the heavens and the earth does not know"; (الغيب) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (إلا) is a particle of exception in the sense of "but" (lākin), indicating that the exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ); (الله) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "knows". It is also correct for (من) to be in the position of the accusative as direct object, (الغيب) being a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) of it and (الله) the agent of (يعلم), the meaning being: say, none knows the things that occur in the heavens and the earth, hidden from us, except Allah the Exalted. The wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; (يشعرون) is an imperfect verb and its agent; (أيان) is an interrogative noun meaning "when", accusative by (يبعثون), and it suspends (يشعرون) from governing, so the clause composed of it and what follows it is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. they are not aware of that. (بَلِ ادَّارَكَ عِلْمُهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ بَلْ هُمْ فِي شَكٍّ مِنْها بَلْ هُمْ مِنْها عَمُونَ): (بل) is a particle of transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī). Al-Jalāl [al-Maḥallī] said it means (هل), which is strange, even though the commentators on al-Jalāl said that al-Jalāl's method is easier than the methods others followed. (ادارك) is a past verb, i.e. it caught up and followed in succession; al-Zamakhsharī cited twelve readings of it. (علمهم) is the agent; (في الآخرة) is attached to (ادارك) or to (علمهم). (ادارك), although past in form, is future in meaning, because it was certain, like His saying «أتى أمر الله». (بل) is also a particle of transitional digression; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and (في شك) the khabar; (منها) is an adjective of (شك). (بل) is also a particle of transitional digression; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ; (منها) is attached to (عمون), and (عمون) is the khabar of (هم). The blindness here is blindness of the heart. The original form is ʿamiyūn: the ḍamma was felt heavy on the yāʾ, so it was transferred to the mīm after its kasra was removed.
(وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَإِذا كُنَّا تُراباً وَآباؤُنا أَإِنَّا لَمُخْرَجُونَ): the wāw is for conjunction; (قال الذين) is a verb and its agent; the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila of (الذين). The hamza is for disapproving interrogation; (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition; the clause (كنا) is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; (كان) and its noun, and (ترابا) is its khabar; (آباؤنا) is conjoined to the noun of (كان), the conjunction to it being permitted by the separation with the khabar. The hamza is also for disapproving interrogation; (إن) and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and (مخرجون) is the khabar of (إن); and the clause is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first clause. (لَقَدْ وُعِدْنا هذا نَحْنُ وَآباؤُنا مِنْ قَبْلُ إِنْ هذا إِلَّا أَساطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ): the clause is a second tawkīd of the preceding clause. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of verification; (وعدنا) is a passive past verb and (نا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (هذا) is the second object of (وعدنا); (نحن) is a tawkīd of (نا); (آباؤنا) is conjoined to the overt pronoun in (وعدنا), the conjunction being permitted by its emphasis with the detached pronoun and by the separation with the second object. (من قبل) is attached to (وعدنا), and the adverb is indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording but not in meaning, i.e. before the coming of Muḥammad, by earlier messengers. Here an ellipsis required by concision must be supplied: "Had what we were promised been true, it would have happened." (إن) is negative; (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (أساطير) is the khabar of (هذا), and (الأولين) is muḍāf ilayhi.
(قُلْ سِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَانْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الْمُجْرِمِينَ): (سيروا) is an imperative verb whose meaning is to threaten them for their denial and to warn them lest there befall them what befell the deniers before them; (في الأرض) is attached to (سيروا); (فانظروا) is conjoined to (سيروا); (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative, the fronted khabar of (كان), and (عاقبة المجرمين) is the postponed noun of (كان). (وَلا تَحْزَنْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلا تَكُنْ فِي ضَيْقٍ مِمَّا يَمْكُرُونَ): the wāw conjoins to (قل); (لا) is prohibitive; (تحزن) is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by (لا), and its agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; (عليهم) is attached to (تحزن); (ولا تكن) is conjoined to (لا تحزن); the noun of (تكن) is latent, its implied form being "you"; (في ضيق) is the khabar; (مما) is an adjective of (ضيق), and the clause (يمكرون) is the ṣila.

* Benefits:
The origin of the confusion in this verse is that they — i.e. the grammarians — parsed the Glorious Name as a badal (substitute) of (من), and in that there is substituting the disconnected excepted, which is a less preferred usage of Tamīm; and since the reading in the nominative is among what the Seven agreed upon, that difficulty arose. In what we have mentioned — i.e. parsing the Glorious Name as a mubtadaʾ — there is an escape from all this. They said: «(الله) is nominative as a badal of (من), because He, the Exalted, is not contained by a place.»
Al-Ṣafāqusī permitted the exception to be connected (muttaṣil), the locative sense in His case, the Exalted, being figurative; in that there is a combination of the literal and the figurative in the locative sense. On this view it is nominative as a badal or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). We have previously set out the combining of the literal and the figurative in one word, and we preferred the permissibility of their combination; on that pattern is their saying «The pen is one of the two tongues». All the scholars of legal theory among the followers of Imam al-Shāfiʿī do not stipulate, for the figurative, the contextual indicator (qarīna) preventing the intention of the literal meaning.
Combining the literal and the figurative involves bringing the speech out contrary to what the apparent situation requires, and it is a kind of rhetorical embellishment (badīʿ) called al-tanwīʿ (diversification): it is the claim that what a word names is of two kinds, conventional and non-conventional, by way of imagination. It is a wide kind that runs through many chapters. Among it is treating what occurs in the place of a thing, as a substitute for it, as having its status, without simile or metaphor, as in their saying «Their greeting among themselves is a painful blow» and their saying «His punishment is the sword».
Ibn al-Kamāl said: If you say, "How is Allah excepted, when He, the Exalted, is far above and exalted beyond being in the heavens and the earth?", I say: just as «غير أن سيوفهم» was excepted in his saying — that is, al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī:
ولا عيب فيهم غير أن سيوفهم ... بهن فلول من قراع الكتائب
(There is no fault in them, except that their swords are notched from clashing with the battalions.)
That is: if Allah the Exalted were among those in the heavens and the earth, then there would be among them one who knows the unseen. The purpose is exaggeration in denying knowledge of the unseen to them and blocking the way to that possibility. So the exception is connected, as in the saying of the Exalted: «ولا تنكحوا ما نكح آباؤكم من النساء إلا ما قد سلف», for the commentators on al-Kashshāf, all of them, stated explicitly that the exception in it is connected.
What is surprising is that al-Bayḍāwī permitted the exception to be connected in the verse on marriage in the manner mentioned, and here was decisive that it is disconnected. What appears from al-Zamakhsharī's words also is decisiveness about its being disconnected, since he said: «It is permissible to put the name of Allah the Exalted in the nominative according to the usage of Banū Tamīm, where they say "There is no one in the house except a donkey", as if "one" had not been mentioned.» For on supplying the speech according to the arrangement mentioned, putting the name of Allah in the nominative is also correct according to the usage of the people of the Ḥijāz.
Some objected to the second parsing — i.e. (من) in the accusative and (الغيب) parsed as a badal ishtimāl of (من) — saying that the badal ishtimāl requires a pronoun as a link, and there is no pronoun here; and the badal is not after the particle of exception, so that it could be said that the strength of the excepted's connection with what it is excepted from makes the pronoun unnecessary. On this basis the first view is free of every objection.

dervis-irab:71-78.t:
* Vocabulary:
(رَدِفَ): In al-Qāmūs: «radifahu, like samiʿa and naṣara: he followed him». But here it has been made to contain (ḍummina) the meaning of danā or qaruba ("drew near"), and for that reason it is made transitive with the lām; or the lām is redundant (zāʾida), as will come in the I'rab. It has also been made transitive with min; he said:
فلما ردفنا من عمير وصحبه ... تولوا سراعا والمنية تعنق
(When we came close upon ʿUmayr and his companions, they turned away in haste, while death sped after them.)
Radifa, like tabiʿa, is transitive by itself, and here it contains the meaning of al-dunuw (drawing near), so it is made transitive with min. Aʿnaqa al-faras: the horse went at a fast, easy pace, and al-ʿanaq is the noun from it. The poet says: when we drew near to ʿUmayr and his companions for battle, they turned their backs hastening, while death was hastening behind them from our side. He likened death to the lion by way of implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya) and attributed al-ʿanaq to it as an imaginative attribution (takhyīl), as if they had followed them by shooting arrows.
It may be that he borrowed "death" for himself and his people by way of explicit metaphor, i.e. "while we were hastening behind them"; then mentioning al-ʿanaq is a tajrīd (abstraction), because it suits the thing likened. Al-ʿanaq is a kind of pace of riding animals, as in al-Ṣiḥāḥ.
Ibn al-Shajarī said:
The meaning of «ردف لكم» is "has followed you"; from it is the ridf of a woman (her buttocks), because it follows her from behind; and from it is the saying of Abū Dhuʾayb:
عاد السواد بياضا في مفارقه ... لا مرحبا ببياض الشيب إذ ردفا
(The black turned to white in the partings of his hair — no welcome to the whiteness of grey hair when it followed on!)
Al-Jawharī said: ardafahu is a dialectal variant of radifahu, like tabiʿahu and atbaʿahu, with the same meaning. Khuzayma ibn Mālik ibn Nahd said:
إذا الجوزاء أردفت الثريا ... ظننت بآل فاطمة الظنونا
(When Gemini followed the Pleiades, I had all manner of thoughts about the family of Fāṭima.)

* I'rab:
(وَيَقُولُونَ مَتى هذَا الْوَعْدُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ): the wāw is resumptive, and the address is to the Prophet. (يقولون) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); (متى) is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as an adverb of time, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate), and (هذا) is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); (الوعد) is a badal (substitute). (إن) is conditional and (كنتم) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (كان) and its noun, and (صادقين) is its khabar; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, what precedes indicating it.
(قُلْ عَسى أَنْ يَكُونَ رَدِفَ لَكُمْ بَعْضُ الَّذِي تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ): (عسى), (لعل) and (سوف), when used in addressing someone of greater standing than you, are tantamount to certainty about what they introduce; they use them only for dignity. (عسى) is a defective (jāmid) past verb, among the verbs of hope; its noun is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it"; (أن يكون) is an interpreted maṣdar, its khabar. The noun of (يكون) is latent, its implied form being "it"; (ردف) is a past verb made to contain the sense of a verb transitive with the lām; (بعض) is the agent and (الذي) is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause (تستعجلون) is the ṣila (relative clause), and the clause (ردف) is the khabar of (يكون). It is said that (ردف) keeps its proper sense, meaning "followed", and the lām is redundant. (وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى النَّاسِ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لا يَشْكُرُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; (إن) and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and (ذو فضل) is its khabar; (على الناس) is attached to (فضل) or is an adjective of it. The wāw is circumstantial; (لكن) is a particle of rectification (istidrāk) that puts in the accusative; (أكثرهم) is its noun and the clause (لا يشكرون) is its khabar. (وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَيَعْلَمُ ما تُكِنُّ صُدُورُهُمْ وَما يُعْلِنُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (إن) and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām, and the clause (يعلم) is the khabar of (إن); (ما) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause (تكن صدورهم) is the ṣila, the referring pronoun being omitted; (وما يعلنون) is conjoined to (ما تكن). (وَما مِنْ غائِبَةٍ فِي السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ إِلَّا فِي كِتابٍ مُبِينٍ): the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; (من) is a redundant preposition; (غائبة) is genitive in wording and nominative in position as a mubtadaʾ, beginning with an indefinite being permitted because negation enters upon it. Al-ghāʾiba is everything hidden: the thing that is absent and concealed is called ghāʾiba and khāfiya, the tāʾ in them having the same status as in al-ʿāfiya, al-ʿāqiba, al-naṣīḥa, al-ramiyya and al-dhabīḥa, in that they are nouns, not adjectives. It is permissible that these be adjectives with the tāʾ in them for intensiveness, like rāwiya, ʿallāma and nassāba. (في السماء والأرض) is an adjective of (غائبة); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (في كتاب) is the khabar of (غائبة), and (مبين) is an adjective. (إِنَّ هذَا الْقُرْآنَ يَقُصُّ عَلى بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ أَكْثَرَ الَّذِي هُمْ فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ): the clause is resumptive, to explain another kind of the distinctions of the Qur'an. (إن) and its noun; (القرآن) is a badal of the demonstrative; the clause (يقص) is the khabar of (إن); (على بني إسرائيل) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يقص); (أكثر) is the direct object and (الذي) is muḍāf ilayhi; (فيه) is attached to (يختلفون), and the clause (يختلفون) is the ṣila of (الذي). [Translator's note: strictly the ṣila is the nominal clause (هم فيه يختلفون), with (يختلفون) as the khabar of (هم); the source states it as written.] (وَإِنَّهُ لَهُدىً وَرَحْمَةٌ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ): conjoined to what precedes; (إن) and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām and (هدى) is its khabar; (رحمة) is conjoined to (هدى); (للمؤمنين) is an adjective. (إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَقْضِي بَيْنَهُمْ بِحُكْمِهِ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْعَلِيمُ): (إن) and its noun, and the clause (يقضي) is its khabar; the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); (بحكمه) is attached to (يقضي); (هو) is a mubtadaʾ, (العزيز) the first khabar and (العليم) the second khabar.

* Benefits:
Rules of the vowelled tāʾ attached to nouns and adjectives:
This tāʾ is one of the signs of the feminine specific to nouns, because, since the feminine is a branch of the masculine, it needed a sign to distinguish it. However, the Arabs have made many nouns feminine with an implied tāʾ, and that implied tāʾ is inferred from the pronoun referring to them, as in «النار وعدها الله الذين كفروا», «حتى تضع الحرب أوزارها» and «إن جنحوا للسلم فاجنح لها»; from pointing to them, as in «هذه جهنم»; and from its appearance in the diminutive of the noun, as in ʿuyayna and udhayna, diminutives of ʿayn (eye) and udhun (ear), among the paired limbs, for the diminutive returns things to their origins. The well-known rule is that among the limbs, what is paired is mostly feminine, except the two eyebrows, the two nostrils and the two cheeks, which are masculine; though the reference point is what is heard from the Arabs, for among the paired is the kaff (palm), which is feminine. Al-Mubarrad claimed that it may be masculine and recited:
ولو كفي اليمين تقيك خوفا ... لأفردت اليمين عن الشمال
(If my right hand were protecting you in fear, I would separate the right from the left.)
But this is a mistake by al-Mubarrad, for al-yamīn stands in the place of al-yumnā, so it is feminine.
Ibn Yasʿūn said: moreover, he returned to the feminine and said «تقيك». We return to the methods of inference and say: the implied tāʾ is also inferred from its appearance in its verb, as in «ولما فصلت العير», and from its absence from its numeral, as in the saying of Ḥumayd al-Arqaṭ describing an Arab bow:
أرمي عليها وهي فرع أجمع ... وهي ثلاث أذرع وأصبع
(I shoot with it while it is all of one top-branch, and it is three cubits and a finger.)
Adhruʿ is the plural of dhirāʿ, which is feminine, as shown by the absence of the tāʾ from its numeral, thalāth. The wāw in his words «وهي» is circumstantial [Translator's note: the source has «فرع للحال», evidently a slip for «للحال»]. One says qaws farʿ when it is made from the top of the branch. By his words «وأصبع» he did not mean literally the measure of a finger, but indicated by it the perfection of the bow, as you say "The cloth is seven cubits and more", meaning that it fully reaches this number.
Mostly this tāʾ serves to separate the feminine adjective from the masculine adjective, like qāʾima and qāʾim; less commonly it is found in nouns that are not adjectives, as in rajul and rajula, ghulām and ghulāma; and in adjectives that bear two intentions, namely adjectives specific to the feminine like ḥāʾiḍ and ṭāmith (menstruating): if what is intended is the occurrence at one of the times, the tāʾ is attached and one says ḥāʾiḍa and ṭāmitha; if that is not intended it is not attached, and one says ḥāʾiḍ and ṭāmith meaning "capable of menstruation".
In al-Mufaṣṣal he said: «The Basrans have two views regarding ḥāʾiḍ and ṭāmith: according to al-Khalīl it is relational (ʿalā al-nasab), like lābin and tāmir, as if it were said "one possessing menstruation"; and according to Sībawayh it is interpreted as "a menstruating person" or "thing", as in their saying ghulām rabʿa, interpreted as nafs. That is only in the permanent attribute; as for the occurring one, it must have the sign of the feminine, so you say "ḥāʾiḍa and ṭāliqa now or tomorrow".» We have explained the difference between the occurring and the permanent attribute in speaking of the saying of the Exalted «يوم ترونها تذهل كل مرضعة عما أرضعت»: the murḍiʿ is she whose role is to nurse, and the murḍiʿa is she who is in the state of nursing, putting her breast into the child's mouth; so look at it there.
In al-Mufaṣṣal he said: «The view of the Kufans is that dropping the tāʾ in ḥāʾiḍ is because there is no need for it.» This would require affirming the tāʾ where there is ambiguity, as in ḍāmir (lean), ʿāshiq (lover), ayyim (unmarried), thayyib (previously married) and ʿānis (spinster); and this objection is clear. As for the objection from affirming the tāʾ in adjectives specific to females, such as imraʾa muṣība and kalba mujriya, according to what is in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, it is not sound, because what they mentioned is permissive, not obligatory, since they say that bringing the tāʾ where it is not needed returns to the original [Translator's note: the source's wording here is elliptical; translated by sense], as with ḥāmila for a woman. Al-Jawharī said in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "One says imraʾa ḥāmil and ḥāmila when she is pregnant. Whoever says ḥāmil says: this is an epithet only for females; and whoever says ḥāmila builds on ḥamalat fa-hiya ḥāmila." And he recited, by ʿAmr ibn Ḥassān:
تمخضت المنون له بيوم ... أتى ولكل حاملة تمام
(Fate went into labour for him with a day that came — and every pregnant one has her term.)
If she carries something on her back or on her head, then she is ḥāmila and nothing else.
Furthermore, this tāʾ does not enter five patterns:
1- faʿūl, with fatḥa on the fāʾ, in the sense of fāʿil, as in rajul jasūr and imraʾa jasūr; «وما كانت أمك بغيّا»; its mention has preceded in Sūrat Maryam.
2- faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl, as in rajul jarīḥ and imraʾa jarīḥ; if you say "I passed by the qatīla of Banū so-and-so", you attach the tāʾ for fear of confusion with the masculine, because you did not mention the qualified noun.
3- mifʿāl, with kasra on the mīm, as in minḥār; one says rajul minḥār and imraʾa minḥār.
4- mifʿīl, with kasra on the mīm, like miʿṭīr from ʿiṭr (perfume); imraʾa miskīna is irregular, and imraʾa miskīn has been heard according to the rule.
5- mifʿal, like mighsham, who is the one who does not desist from what he wants and desires, out of his courage.
The tāʾ of separation: the tāʾ comes to separate a single unit from the genus, like tamra and tamr, or to separate the genus from the single unit, as in kamʾa [Translator's note: the source has «كماة»]; and sayyāra in the saying of the Exalted «وجاءت سيارة» is not of this, for it is the plural of sayyār, not one of the generic nouns.
The tāʾ of compensation: it is the one that comes as compensation for a fāʾ, as in ʿida; or an ʿayn, as in iqāma; or a lām, as in sana; or for an extra letter not carrying meaning, as in zindīq and zanādiqa, where the tāʾ is compensation for the yāʾ of zanādīq.
The tāʾ of Arabicisation: it is the one that comes to Arabicise foreign nouns, as in mawāzija, plural of mawzaj — with fatḥa on the mīm, sukūn on the wāw, fatḥa on the zāy, followed by jīm — which is the khuff (leather sock) or the stocking; the regular form would be mawāzij, and the tāʾ entered its plural to indicate that its origin is foreign and it was Arabicised.
The tāʾ of intensiveness: the tāʾ of intensiveness in description, like rāwiya for one who transmits a great deal, and nassāba for one with great knowledge of genealogies.

dervis-irab:15-19.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَنْطِقَ الطَّيْرِ): «المنطق» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) of «نطق ينطق», of the pattern of ḍaraba: nuṭqan, manṭiqan and nuṭūqan, i.e., he spoke with sound and letters by which meanings are known. «المنطق» is speech, and it is sometimes used of other than humans: one says "I heard the manṭiq of the birds." Al-Bayḍāwī said: «Nuṭq and manṭiq in common usage are every utterance by which what is in the mind is expressed, whether single or compound, meaningful or not meaningful. It is sometimes applied to everything that makes a sound, by likening or by extension, as in their saying "the dove spoke (naṭaqat)"; and from it come "the speaking and the silent" for animals and inanimate things. For animal sounds, inasmuch as they follow imaginings, are given the status of expressions, especially as some of them vary with the variation of purposes, so that those of their own kind understand them.»
Al-Zamakhsharī added to what al-Bayḍāwī said: «Yaʿqūb ibn al-Sikkīt entitled his book Iṣlāḥ al-Manṭiq (The Correction of Speech), and he corrected in it nothing but single words.»
It appears that the etymological origin of the word «المنطق» shows us the close connection between thought and language: the thinking animal alone is the speaking animal. Language is not merely a tool that the human mind has fashioned to express its purposes and aims; it is also a means of abstracting from sensory accidents and fashioning certain symbols or abstract significations.
The science of logic (ʿilm al-manṭiq) is a science that investigates sound and corrupt thinking. It lays down the rules that protect the mind from falling into errors in judgments, and it is also concerned with knowing the various methods [of scholars] in their many studies and diverse researches. It is true that the subject of logic is human thinking in general, but logic is not limited to describing the mental operations we perform when we think, judge, abstract, remember or solve a problem; it also seeks to help us distinguish between the correct judgment and the mistaken one, between sound inference and corrupt inference.
The ancient Greek philosophers were concerned with studying the relationship between the form of thought and its matter, i.e., between the formal aspect of judgments or propositions and the content of thinking itself; from that arose dialectical inquiries which were the first nucleus of the science of logic. Thus Socrates and Plato were concerned with investigating the fallacies of the Sophists, and to refute them they laid down the principles of sound dialectical thinking. Then came Aristotle, who benefited from the studies of those before him in forming concepts, logical division and the methods of presenting proof, and he put all this into a famous book called "the Prior Analytics". And although Aristotle did not use the word "logic", the historians agree in pledging allegiance to him as the prince of logic.
In modern times, both Bacon and Descartes rebelled against Aristotle's logic, claiming that it is a barren formal logic. Then the logicians finally realized the necessity of freeing thought from the magic of words and liberating it from the authority of language, and they tried to make logic a mathematical science that formulates mental operations in algebraic symbols.
(يُوزَعُونَ): the first of them are held back for the last of them, i.e., the vanguard (sullāf) of the army is halted until those following catch up with them; «سلاف العسكر» means their foremost, as in al-Ṣiḥāḥ. In al-Mukhtār: «وزعه يزعه وزعا, like وضعه يضعه وضعا, i.e., he restrained him, and اتّزع, i.e., he refrained. أوزعه بالشيء: he incited him to it. استوزعت الله شكره فأوزعني: I asked Allah to inspire me to thank Him, and He inspired me. Al-wāziʿ is the one who goes ahead of the rank and sets it in order, moving some forward and some back; its plural is wazaʿa. Al-Ḥasan said: "People must have a wāziʿ", i.e., an authority that restrains them. One says وزعت الجيش when you hold back the first of the army for the last of it.»
(نَمْلَةٌ): «النمل» and «النمُل» (with ḍamma on the mīm): a creature eager to gather food; it makes villages under the ground in which there are dwellings, corridors, chambers and winding storeys which it fills with grain and provisions for the winter. The singular is «نملة» and «نمُلة», for male and female, and the plural is «نمال».
Al-Zamakhsharī related of Abū Ḥanīfa that he stood by Qatāda while he was saying: "Ask me." Abū Ḥanīfa ordered a person to ask Qatāda about Solomon's ant: was it male or female? He did not answer. Abū Ḥanīfa was asked about that and said: "It was female," and he argued from the attachment of the marker [of the feminine]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «That is because «النملة» is like «الحمامة» and «الشاة» in applying to the male and the female, and they are distinguished by a marker, as in "a male dove" and "a female dove".»
[Translator's note: what follows appears to be a quotation of an objection to this report (it resembles the words of Abū Ḥayyān/Ibn al-Munayyir), though the source does not mark it as such.] I do not know which to marvel at more: him, or Abū Ḥanīfa, that this should be established as coming from him. For «النملة», like «الحمامة» and «الشاة», applies to the male and the female, because it is a generic noun: one says «نملة ذكر» and «نملة أنثى» as one says «حمامة ذكر» and «حمامة أنثى», «شاة ذكر» and «شاة أنثى». Its word is feminine and its meaning is open, so it may be treated as feminine for the sake of its word even though it applies to a male; indeed this is the eloquent, current usage. Do you not see his words, upon him be blessings and peace: "No one-eyed, emaciated or blind [animal] is to be sacrificed" — how he put these adjectives in the feminine according to the word, without meaning the females of livestock specifically? So in the words of the Exalted «نملة», the femininity of the word was observed, while the meaning is equally open [to both]. More of this discussion will come in the Benefits section.
(أَوْزِعْنِي): inspire me. Its literal sense is: make me restrain (azaʿu) gratitude for Your favour to me, hold it back and tie it fast, so that it does not escape me, so that I never cease to be grateful to You. The explanation of this root has preceded.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا داوُدَ وَسُلَيْمانَ عِلْماً): the wāw is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, to begin the second story, the story of David and Solomon. The lām paves the way for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); «قد» is a particle of realization; «آتينا» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «داود» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), «سليمان» is conjoined to «داود», and «علما» is a second direct object.
(وَقالا الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي فَضَّلَنا عَلى كَثِيرٍ مِنْ عِبادِهِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction, and «قالا» is conjoined to something implied, its implied form being: "so they acted upon what they were given, with the heart by resolve, with the limbs by practice, and with the tongue, and they said". «الحمد» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «لله» its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). «الذي» is a relative noun, an adjective of «الله»; the clause «فضلنا» is the ṣila (relative clause); «على كثير» are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «فضلنا»; «من عباده» is an adjective of «كثير», and «المؤمنين» an adjective of «عباده».
(وَوَرِثَ سُلَيْمانُ داوُدَ وَقالَ يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ عُلِّمْنا مَنْطِقَ الطَّيْرِ): the wāw is resumptive; «ورث سليمان داود» is a verb, its agent and its direct object; «قال» is conjoined to «ورث»; the i'rab of «يا أيها الناس» has preceded. «علمنا» is a passive past verb, «نا» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and «منطق الطير» is a second direct object.
(وَأُوتِينا مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ إِنَّ هذا لَهُوَ الْفَضْلُ الْمُبِينُ): «أوتينا» is conjoined to «علمنا»; «من كل شيء» are attached to «أوتينا». «إن هذا»: «إن» and its noun — it is resumptive speech, brought by way of expressing thanks and praise. The lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «هو» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ; «الفضل» is the khabar of «إن» or the khabar of «هو», the clause being the khabar of «إن»; and «المبين» is an adjective of «الفضل».
(وَحُشِرَ لِسُلَيْمانَ جُنُودُهُ مِنَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ وَالطَّيْرِ فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; «حشر» is a passive past verb; «لسليمان» are attached to «حشر»; «جنوده» is the deputy agent; «من الجن والإنس والطير» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «جنوده». The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; «هم» is a mubtadaʾ and the clause «يوزعون» its khabar. What history relates about Solomon's camp will come in the Rhetoric section.
(حَتَّى إِذا أَتَوْا عَلى وادِ النَّمْلِ قالَتْ نَمْلَةٌ يا أَيُّهَا النَّمْلُ ادْخُلُوا مَساكِنَكُمْ): «حتى» is a particle of limit for something omitted, its implied form being "so they went on until, when they came…". It may also be the limit of «يوزعون», because it includes the sense of "they travel, some of them prevented from separating from others, until when they came…". «على وادي النمل» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «أتوا»; the secret of attaching it to «أتوا» will come in the Rhetoric section. The clause «قالت نملة» has no grammatical position; the i'rab of «يا أيها النمل» has preceded. «ادخلوا مساكنكم» is a verb, its agent and its direct object by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa). What al-Suyūṭī said in al-Itqān about the ant's words will come.
(لا يَحْطِمَنَّكُمْ سُلَيْمانُ وَجُنُودُهُ وَهُمْ لا يَشْعُرُونَ): a resumptive prohibition with no connection to what precedes it, i.e., "do not be where they would crush you". The speech may also be a badal (substitute) of the command clause similar to it, namely «ادخلوا مساكنكم».
Al-Zamakhsharī addressed this expression and said: «If you say: what is «لا يحطمنكم»? I say: it may be a reply to the command, or a prohibition that is a badal of the command. What permits it to be a badal of it is that it carries the sense of "do not be where you are, so that he crushes you", in the manner [Translator's note: the source prints «طريقه», evidently for «طريقة»] of «لا أرينك هاهنا» (let me not see you here).» «لا» is the prohibitive lā; «يحطمنكم» is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of jussive by «لا»; the kāf is the direct object; «سليمان» is the agent and «جنوده» is conjoined to «سليمان». «وهم»: the wāw is of ḥāl, «هم» a mubtadaʾ and the clause «لا يشعرون» its khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl.
(فَتَبَسَّمَ ضاحِكاً مِنْ قَوْلِها): the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted that the context requires, i.e., "so he heard her aforementioned words and smiled". «ضاحكا» is an emphasizing ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida); the secret of what made him laugh will come in the Benefits section. «من قولها» are attached to «ضاحكا».
(وَقالَ رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِي أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيَّ وَعَلى والِدَيَّ): «قال» is conjoined to «فتبسم». «رب» is one addressed (munādā), annexed to the yāʾ of the speaker, which is omitted, and the vocative particle is omitted. «أوزعني» is a verb of supplication, a latent (mustatir) agent and a direct object. «أن» with what falls in its scope is the second object of «أوزعني», because it includes the sense of inspiring; or it is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e., «بأن أشكر نعمتك». «التي» is an adjective of «نعمتك»; the clause «أنعمت» is the ṣila; «عليّ» are attached to «أنعمت», and «على والدي» is conjoined to «عليّ».
(وَأَنْ أَعْمَلَ صالِحاً تَرْضاهُ): a conjoined clause.
(وَأَدْخِلْنِي بِرَحْمَتِكَ فِي عِبادِكَ الصَّالِحِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; «أدخلني» is a verb of supplication, its agent and its direct object; «برحمتك» are attached to an omitted ḥāl, the bāʾ being causal; «في عبادك» are attached to «أدخلني», and «الصالحين» is a naʿt (adjective) of «عبادك».

* Rhetoric:
These verses contain various arts, which we set out below:
1- Indefiniteness and its secrets:
In His words «وقد آتينا داود وسليمان علما» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse reads «ولقد»] there is indefiniteness, whose benefit is to convey partiality and paucity, or to convey magnification and abundance; the second is what is meant here. The apparent sense of His words «ولقد آتينا داود وسليمان علما», in the context of conferring favour, is the magnification of the knowledge they were given, as if He said: knowledge — and what knowledge! And so it was, for their knowledge was of a kind found strange and great, including knowledge of the speech of birds and of the other animals; although every knowledge, compared with the knowledge of Allah, is little and slight.
A wonderful story:
We give here a related story, following our custom of including related stories so that they may be a source of inspiration for writers and landmarks of daylight for them. Muqātil said: Solomon was sitting in his camp, whose area was a hundred parasangs by a hundred: twenty-five for the jinn, twenty-five for humans, twenty-five for the birds and twenty-five for the wild beasts. The jinn had woven for him a carpet of gold and silk, a parasang by a parasang. A bird passed by him circling — and in one report he saw a nightingale on a tree — and he said to those sitting with him: "Do you know what this bird says?" They said: "Allah and His Prophet know best." He said: "It says: I have eaten half a date, so may the world perish." He passed by a hoopoe on top of a tree and said: "[It says:] Ask Allah's forgiveness, O sinners." A ring-dove cried, and he told them that it says: "Would that these creatures had not been created." A peacock cried, and he said it says: "As you judge, so shall you be judged." A ṭīṭawā [a sandpiper-like bird] cried, and he said it says: "Every living thing will die, and every new thing will wear out." A swallow cried, and he said it says: "Send forward good and you will find it." A turtle-dove cried, and he told them that it says: "Glory be to my Lord the Most High." He said: the kite says: "Everything perishes except His Face"; the sandgrouse says: "Whoever keeps silent is safe"; the parrot says: "Woe to the one whose concern is the world"; the cock says: "Remember Allah, O heedless ones"; the vulture says: "O son of Adam, live as long as you will; your end is death"; the eagle says: "In distance from people there is companionship [with Allah]"; and the frog says: "Glory be to my Lord the Most High."
2- The use of the preposition:
He said «حتى إذا أتوا على وادي النمل», making «أتوا» transitive with «على», because the coming was from above, so He used the particle of superiority (istiʿlāʾ). Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī glimpsed this lofty sky and said:
فلشد ما جاوزت قدرك صاعد ... ولشدّ ما قربت عليك الأنجم
(How far you have overstepped your worth, climbing! How near the stars have come to you!)
By "the stars" he meant the verses of his poetry. He says: how greatly you have overstepped your worth, sending to ask me for praise! Your asking me to praise you is an overstepping of your worth on your part, since you sought that the stars descend from their heavens to come near you. This verse is among the most stinging and foul-mouthed of satire. It is from an ode by Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī [Translator's note: the source prints «المتبني» here]. He had travelled from al-Ramla intending Antioch and stopped at Tripoli, where Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Aʿwar ibn Kayghalagh was; he was ignorant, and three men of the Banū Ḥaydara used to sit with him, between whom and Abū al-Ṭayyib there was an old enmity. They said to him: "Would you like him to pass you by and not praise you?" and they kept inciting him. So he sent to him asking that he praise him, and Abū al-Ṭayyib excused himself by an oath binding him not to praise anyone for a period. So he held him back from his journey to wait out the period, and took the road from him and controlled it. The three men who had been inciting him died within forty days. Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī then satirized him and dictated the poem to someone he trusted. When the snow melted, he went out as if exercising his horse and travelled to Damascus. Ibn Kayghalagh sent horsemen and footmen after him, but he escaped them, and the ode became known. Its beginning is:
لهوى النفوس سريرة لا تعلم ... عرضا نظرت وخلت أني أسلم
(The passion of souls has a secret that is not known; I glanced by chance and thought I would be safe.)
Among its verses of wisdom:
ولقد رأيت الحادثات فلا أرى ... يققا يميت ولا سوادا يعصم
(I have seen the events of fortune, and I see neither white hair that kills nor black hair that protects.)
والهم يخترم الجسيم نحافة ... ويشيب ناصية الصبيّ ويهرم
(Worry wastes the stout body into leanness, whitens the forelock of the boy and makes him old.)
ذو العقل يشقى في النعيم بعقله ... وأخو الجهالة في الشقاوة ينعم
(The man of intelligence is wretched amid bliss because of his intelligence, while the brother of ignorance lives in comfort amid wretchedness.)
والناس قد نبذوا الحفاظ فمطلق ... ينسى الذي يولى وعاف يندم
(People have cast off loyalty: the one released forgets the favour done him, and the one who pardons regrets it.)
لا يخدعنّك من عدوّ دمعه ... وارحم شبابك من عدوّ ترحم
(Let not an enemy's tear deceive you; have mercy on your youth from an enemy you pity.)
لا يسلم الشرف الرفيع من الأذى ... حتّى يراق على جوانبه الدّم
(Lofty honour is not safe from harm until blood is shed around it.)
والظلم من شيم النفوس فإن تجد ... داعفة فلعلّة لا يظلم
(Injustice is part of the nature of souls; if you find one who is chaste, it is for some reason that he does not do wrong.) [Translator's note: the source prints «داعفة»; the familiar text is «ذا عفة».]
Then he turned to satirizing Ibn Kayghalagh, and was foul-mouthed:
يحمي ابن كيغلغ الطريق وعرسه ... ما بين رجليها الطريق الأعظم
(Ibn Kayghalagh guards the road, while his wife… [an obscene insult about her unchastity].)
أقم المسالح وق شفر سكينة ... إن المنيّ بحلقتيها خضرم
(Station your guards over Sukayna's [obscene sexual insult].) [Translator's note: the source prints «وق», evidently for «فوق».]
وارفق بنفسك إنّ خلقك ناقص ... واستر أباك فإنّ أصلك مظلم
(Go easy on yourself, for your make is deficient; and hide your father, for your origin is dark.)
واحذر مناوأة الرجال فإنما ... تقوى على كسر العبيد وتقدم
(Beware of contending with men, for you are only strong and bold enough to break slaves.)
وغناك مسألة وطيشك نفخة ... ورضاك فيشلة وربك درهم
(Your wealth is from begging, your rashness mere bluster, your satisfaction [an obscene word], and your lord a dirham.)
Then he returns to fitting wisdom, saying:
ومن البلية عذل من لا يرعوي ... عن غيّه وخطاب من لا يفهم
(It is an affliction to reproach one who will not desist from his error, and to address one who does not understand.)
[Translator's note: from here the lines are broken across lines in the source; they are given as whole verses with the text unchanged.]
يمشي بأربعة على أعقابه ... تحت العلوج ومن وراء يلجم
(He walks on all fours backwards beneath the louts, and is bridled from behind.)
وجفونه ما تستقر كأنها ... مطروفة أو فتّ فيها حصرم
(His eyelids never stay still, as if they had been struck in the eye or sour grapes crumbled into them.)
وإذا أشار محدثا فكأنه ... قرد يقهقه أو عجوز تلصم
(When he gestures while talking, it is as if he were a cackling ape or an old woman slapping [her face].) [Translator's note: «تلصم» is as printed; the familiar text is «تلطم».]
يقلى مفارقة الأكفّ قذاله ... حتى يكاد على يد يتعمّم
(His nape hates to be parted from slapping hands, so much that he almost wears a turban of hands.)
وتراه أصغر ما تراه ناطقا ... ويكون أكذب ما يكون ويقسم
(You see him at his smallest when speaking, and he is at his most lying when he swears.)
والذل يظهر في الذليل مودة ... وأودّ منه لمن يودّ الأرقم
(Abasement shows itself in the abased as affection; but the speckled viper is more loving than he to one who loves it.)
ومن العداوة ما ينالك نفعه ... ومن الصداقة ما يضر ويؤلم
(There is enmity whose benefit reaches you, and friendship that harms and hurts.)
The whole ode is of this splendid kind; what we have given of it suffices us. Returning to what we were dealing with, we say: it may also mean crossing the valley and reaching its end, from their saying «أتى على الشيء» when one reaches its end.
3- Tawlīd (generation of figures):
The verse «قالت نملة يا أيها النمل ادخلوا مساكنكم لا يحطمنكم سليمان وجنوده وهم لا يشعرون» contains eleven kinds of rhetoric, some generated from others, which al-Suyūṭī mentioned in his book al-Itqān. That is, she spoke words containing letters and sounds, and what is meant is that she said it by way of good counsel; and these words of hers contained eleven kinds of rhetoric:
First: the call with «يا».
Second: she used an indirect designation with «أي».
Third: she gave notice with the hāʾ of alerting (hāʾ al-tanbīh).
Fourth: she named, by saying «النمل».
Fifth: she commanded, by saying «ادخلوا».
Sixth: she specified, by saying «مساكنهم» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse reads «مساكنكم»].
Seventh: she warned, by saying «لا يحطمنكم».
Eighth: she particularized, by saying «سليمان».
Ninth: she generalized, by saying «وجنوده».
Tenth: she pointed, by saying «وهم».
Eleventh: she excused, by saying «لا يشعرون».
They also recited, posing a riddle about Solomon's ant and the cow of the Children of Israel:
فما ميت أحيا له الله ميتا ... ليخبر قوما أنذروا ببيان
(What dead thing was it for whose sake Allah brought a dead man to life, to inform a people who were warned plainly?)
وعجفاء قد قامت لتنذر قومها ... واهل قراها رهبة الحدثان
(And a lean female who rose to warn her people and the folk of her villages for fear of calamity?)

* Benefits:
1- What made Solomon laugh?
Solomon laughed at the ant's words for two reasons:
The first: what indicated the evident mercy of him and his soldiers and their compassion, namely her saying «وهم لا يشعرون», meaning that if they were aware they would not do it.
The second: his joy at what Allah had given him, which He had given no one else: his hearing perceiving what the ant said, though it is proverbial for smallness and insignificance. When a person sees or hears something he has no acquaintance with, he laughs.
2- The explanatory and the emphasizing ḥāl:
The ḥāl is of two kinds: founding (muʾassisa), also called explanatory (mubayyina), whose meaning cannot be obtained without it, as in «جاء زيد راكبا» (Zayd came riding), where the meaning of riding is obtained only by mentioning «راكبا»; and emphasizing (muʾakkida), whose meaning is obtained without mentioning it. The latter is divided into three kinds:
a- Emphasizing its governing word in wording and meaning, as in «وأرسلناك للناس رسولا»: «رسولا» is a ḥāl of the kāf, and it emphasizes its governing word «أرسلنا» in wording and meaning.
b- Emphasizing its governing word in meaning only, the wording being different, as in «فتبسم ضاحكا»: «ضاحكا» is a ḥāl of the agent of «تبسم», and it emphasizes its governing word in meaning only, because smiling is a kind of laughing, while the wording is different.
c- Emphasizing its owner (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl), as in «لآمن من في الأرض كلهم جميعا»: «جميعا» is a ḥāl of the agent of «آمن», namely the relative «من», emphasizing it. There are other kinds of the emphasizing ḥāl, for which the extensive works should be consulted.

dervis-irab:79-82.t:
* I'rab:
(فَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ إِنَّكَ عَلَى الْحَقِّ الْمُبِينِ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition), because it is a consequence drawn from His saying «العزيز العليم», i.e. if you have come to know these attributes of Allah the Exalted and believe in them, then rely. (توكل) is an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; (على الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (توكل). The clause (إنك على الحق المبين) has no grammatical position, because it gives the reason for the reliance; (إن), its noun and its khabar (predicate); (المبين) is an adjective. (إِنَّكَ لا تُسْمِعُ الْمَوْتى وَلا تُسْمِعُ الصُّمَّ الدُّعاءَ إِذا وَلَّوْا مُدْبِرِينَ): a second reason for the command to rely; it cuts off his hope of their following him. (إن) and its noun, and the clause (لا تسمع) is the khabar; (الموتى) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (ولا تسمع الصم) is conjoined to the one before it; (الصم) is the first direct object and (الدعاء) the second direct object. (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition; the clause (ولوا) is in the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; (مدبرين) is a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَما أَنْتَ بِهادِي الْعُمْيِ عَنْ ضَلالَتِهِمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negative that operates like (ليس); (أنت) is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and (هادي) is genitive in wording and accusative in position as the khabar of (ما); (العمي) is muḍāf ilayhi; (عن ضلالتهم) is attached to (هادي), made transitive with (عن) because it contains the meaning of "turning them away". Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted another view, namely that it is attached to (العمي), because you say «عمي عن كذا» ("he was blind to such-and-such"), and it is a permissible, acceptable view. Al-Zamakhsharī illustrated the first view with their saying «سقاه عن العيمة», i.e. he kept him away from it by giving him drink; al-ʿayma is the craving for milk, as in al-Ṣiḥāḥ. (إِنْ تُسْمِعُ إِلَّا مَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِآياتِنا فَهُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ): (إن) is negative; (تسمع) is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (من) is the direct object, and the clause (يؤمن) is the ṣila (relative clause); (بآياتنا) is attached to (يؤمن); the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (مسلمون) the khabar.
(وَإِذا وَقَعَ الْقَوْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ أَخْرَجْنا لَهُمْ دَابَّةً مِنَ الْأَرْضِ): the wāw is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, introduced to set out some of the signs of the Hour that point to it. What is meant by "the word" is what the Qur'an has pronounced of the verses that tell of the Hour, and what is meant by its "falling", though it has not yet fallen, is the nearness of its occurrence. (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition; the clause (وقع القول) is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; (القول) is the agent of (وقع); (عليهم) is attached to (وقع). The clause (أخرجنا) has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition; (لهم) is attached to (أخرجنا); (دابة) is the direct object; (من الأرض) is an adjective of (دابة). What has been said about the Beast of the Earth will come in the Benefits section.
(تُكَلِّمُهُمْ أَنَّ النَّاسَ كانُوا بِآياتِنا لا يُوقِنُونَ): the clause (تكلمهم) is a second adjective of (دابة), or a ḥāl of it because it has been qualified. (أن) with fatḥa on the hamza is on the supposition of the bāʾ, i.e. «بأن الناس», and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (تكلمهم); it was read with kasra as resumptive. (أن) and its noun, and the clause (كانوا) is the khabar of (أن); (كان) and its noun; (بآياتنا) is attached to (يوقنون); (لا) is negative, and the clause (لا يوقنون) is the khabar of (كانوا). The speech is either from Allah the Exalted or part of the speech of the Beast. Al-Zamakhsharī chose this latter view, and replied to those who objected that His saying «بآياتنا» disturbs that: that its saying is a report of the saying of Allah the Exalted, or is in the sense of "the signs of our Lord", or that, because of its special relation to Allah and its favour with Him, and its being among His select creatures, it annexed Allah's signs to itself, just as some of a king's intimates say "our horses" and "our lands", when they are only the horses and lands of their master.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «ولا تسمع الصم الدعاء إذا ولوا مدبرين» there is the device of īghāl (pressing beyond), which is that the speaker completes the meaning of his speech before bringing its ending, and when he wishes to bring it, he brings what conveys a meaning additional to the meaning of that speech. The speech ended at His words «ولا تسمع الصم الدعاء», so what is the meaning of His words «ولوا مدبرين»? The answer is that He brought it although mentioning the turning away apparently made it unnecessary; but in reality it did not make it unnecessary, because turning away may be with one side rather than another, as aversion may be. Since He, Glorified is He, reported their turning away to complete the meaning in the situation of being addressed — to deny them the understanding that comes from gesture, for the deaf man understands from gesture what the hearer understands from words — then He, Glorified is He, knew that turning away may be with one side rather than another, as we stated, so it is possible for him to glance with the side with which he did not turn, and so grasp some of the gesture; and what is meant is the negation of all gesture. So the verse-ending «مدبرين» came, so that it is known that the turning away was with all sides, such that what had been facing became turned away, and the one addressed was screened from the addresser, since he became behind him; so the gesture was hidden from his unseen just as his ears were deaf to words, and complete exaggeration was achieved in not making him hear at all. This is a representation (tamthīl) by which the state of these people was represented, coming embedded in the īghāl, and this type of īghāl is called the īghāl of precaution (al-iḥtiyāṭ).
There is another type, namely the īghāl of choice (al-takhyīr), whose example has passed in Sūrat al-Māʾida; we have presented in al-Māʾida sufficient examples of īghāl, and we cite here some samples of it. It is related that when Laylā's brothers learned of Tawba ibn al-Ḥumayyir al-ʿUqaylī's love for her, they vowed to shed his blood and moved away with her, so Tawba said:
وان يمنعوا ليلى وحسن حديثها ... فلن يمنعوا عني البكا والقوافيا
فهلا منعتم إذ منعتم حديثها ... خيالا يوافيني مع الليل هاديا
(If they withhold Laylā and her lovely talk, they will not withhold weeping and rhymes from me. Since you withheld her talk, why did you not withhold a phantom that comes to me with the night, guiding its way?)
The meaning was complete with his words «مع الليل», and when he brought the rhyme he added to that.
And by Abū Tammām:
إن المنازل ساورتها فرقة ... أخلت من الآرام كل كناس
من كل ضاحكة الترائب أرهفت ... إرهاف خوط البانة المياس
(The dwellings were assailed by a parting that emptied every covert of its white gazelles — every one with gleaming breast, made slender as the slenderness of the swaying willow-wand.)
The meaning was complete before he brought the rhyme in the second verse, and when he brought it he added to it. In this fine manner it runs consistently for him, and he says:
فتوح أمير المؤمنين تفتحت ... لهن أزاهير الربا والخمائل
لقد ألبس الله الإمام فضائلا ... وتابع فيها باللها والفواضل
فأضحت عطاياه نوازع شردا ... تسائل في الآفاق عن كل سائل
مواهب جدن الأرض حتى كأنما ... أخذن بآداب السحاب الهواطل
(For the conquests of the Commander of the Faithful the blossoms of the hills and thickets have opened. Allah has clothed the Imam with virtues and followed them with gifts and bounties, so that his gifts became roaming strays, asking in the horizons after every asker — endowments that rained generously on the earth, as if they had taken on the manners of the pouring clouds.)

* Benefits:
The Beast of the Earth:
The Beast of the Earth is al-Jassāsa; its tanwīn and indefiniteness are to make its magnification vague, so as to draw attention to it and turn eyes to awaiting its emergence. Much has been said about it in the lengthy works; it is among the matters of the unseen in which we believe, and its essence and reality do not concern us.

dervis-irab:83-88.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فَوْجاً): al-fawj is the group and the party; its plural is afwāj and fuʾūj, and the plural of the plural afāwij, afāyij and afāwīj. Al-fāʾija is the group, and also the open space between any two elevations of sand or rough ground. Al-Rāghib said in his Mufradāt:
«Al-fawj is the group passing by in haste; it seems this is the original sense, then it was applied even when there is no passing or haste. The plural is afwāj and fuʾūj.»
(يُوزَعُونَ): it has preceded recently in Sūrat al-Naḥl [Translator's note: so in the source; the word occurs earlier in this sūra, al-Naml, verse 17], so renew your acquaintance with it; i.e. the first of them are held back for the last of them so that they catch up with one another.
(داخِرِينَ): humbled. In al-Qāmūs: dakhara al-shakhṣ, like manaʿa and fariḥa, dakhran and dukhūran: he became small and abased; and adkhartuhu, with the alif, for transitivity. The dāl with the khāʾ, as the first and second radicals, convey a particular meaning indicating shrinking, self-abasement, and what the soul recoils from and natures find nauseating. Al-dukh and al-dakh is smoke, which is well known to blind the eyes and irritate them. A Bedouin woman said of her husband, who had grown old and aged:
لاخير في الشيخ إذا ما اجلخّا ... وسال غرب عينيه ولخّا
وكان أكلا قاعدا وشخّا ... تحت رواق البيت يغشى الدّخا
وانثنت الرجل فصارت فخّا ... وصار وصل الغانيات أخّا
(There is no good in an old man when he collapses, the stream of his eyes runs and is bleary, his eating and his pissing are done sitting under the tent's awning, frequenting the smoke; his leg has bent and become a snare, and union with beautiful women has become "ugh!")
The meaning of «يغشى الدخ» is that he frequently goes back and forth to the women at the oven, saying "Feed me". The meaning of ijlakhkha is: he fell down and did not move; and it is said its meaning is: he became bent. Akh, with fatḥa on the hamza, is a word said when groaning; thus said Ibn Durayd, who then said: "I reckon it is post-classical." Al-Ṣāghānī said: to a child, when he is forbidden from doing something dirty, one says ikh, with kasra on the hamza, equivalent to the Persians saying kikh, as if it were a rebuke; and its hamza may be given fatḥa. Dakhdakha al-rajul: the man took short steps in haste; tadakhdakha al-rajul: the man shrank. Dakhasa al-shayʾ fī al-ramād: he put the thing into the ashes and buried it; dukhisa al-ḥāfir: the hoof was afflicted by al-dakhas, which is a swelling in the hoof of a riding animal; and al-dukhas, with ḍamma on the dāl, is a sea creature. Dakhala is well known, and it conveys concealment and shrinking. Dukhila fī ʿaqlihi, in the passive, or in his body, and dakhila, with kasra on the khāʾ, dakhalan with two fatḥas: corruption entered him, so he is madkhūl ʿalayhi. Al-dakhl, with fatḥa on the dāl and sukūn on the khāʾ, is what comes in to you of your wealth for you to store and hide from eyes, and also illness and defect. Al-dakhal, with two fatḥas, is what enters a person of corruption in the mind and body, deception, and defect in lineage. Al-dakhīl is one who enters among a people and claims descent from them though not of them, plural dukhalāʾ; and every foreign word. One says dāʾ dakhīl, i.e. an illness that has entered the depths of the body; and one says "He is of wicked dikhla" — with kasra on the doubled dāl — which is the inner side of his affair. Dakhamahu dakhman: he pushed him roughly. Dakhina al-ṭaʿām wal-laḥm, of the taʿiba pattern: smoke affected them while cooking, and nothing is fouler than its taste then. How many marvels this language has!

* I'rab:
(وَيَوْمَ نَحْشُرُ مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ فَوْجاً مِمَّنْ يُكَذِّبُ بِآياتِنا فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ): the wāw is resumptive, and the adverb is attached to something omitted, its implied form being "remember"; it is resumptive speech, introduced to show the conditions of the liars in summary form. The clause (نحشر) is in the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; (من كل أمة) is attached to (نحشر), and (من) here is partitive; (فوجا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (ممن) is an adjective of (فوجا), and (من) here is explicative (for clarification); the clause (يكذب) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (من). The fāʾ is a conjunction; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause (يوزعون) is the khabar (predicate).
(حَتَّى إِذا جاؤُ قالَ أَكَذَّبْتُمْ بِآياتِي وَلَمْ تُحِيطُوا بِها عِلْماً أَمَّا ذا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ): (حتى) is a particle of limit; (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition; the clause (جاءوا) is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it, and what (جاءوا) is attached to is omitted, i.e. to the place of reckoning. (قال) is a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), referring back to Allah the Exalted. (أكذبتم): the hamza is for rebuking, reproaching interrogation, and (كذبتم) is a verb and its agent; (بآياتي) is attached to (كذبتم). In (ولم) the wāw is circumstantial and (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and jussive; (تحيطوا) is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by (لم); (بها) is attached to (تحيطوا); (علما) is a tamyīz (specification); the clause is circumstantial, emphasising the disapproval and rebuke and showing the hideousness of the denial based on improvisation and the lack of reflection, insight and verification. (أم) is a conjunction, and here it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), so it means (بل); (ما) is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and (ذا) is a relative noun, the khabar; or (ماذا) as a whole is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative, the fronted object of (تعملون). (كنتم): (كان) and its noun, and the clause (تعملون) is its khabar. (وَوَقَعَ الْقَوْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ بِما ظَلَمُوا فَهُمْ لا يَنْطِقُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (وقع القول) is a verb and its agent; (عليهم) is attached to (وقع), and (بما ظلموا) is also attached to (وقع), i.e. because of their wrongdoing, (ما) being maṣdariyya. The fāʾ is a conjunction; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (لا ينطقون) is the khabar.
(أَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا جَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِيَسْكُنُوا فِيهِ وَالنَّهارَ مُبْصِراً إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ): the hamza is for affirmative and disapproving interrogation; (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion and jussive; (يروا) is an imperfect verb in the jussive by (لم). The seeing here is mental, not visual; (أن) and what follows it stand in place of the two objects of (يروا). (أن) and its noun, and the clause (جعلنا) is its khabar. The making (al-jaʿl) here, if it is in the sense of creating, not of transforming, is transitive to one object, and (الليل) is the object of (جعلنا). The lām is for causation; (يسكنوا) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied an after the lām of causation, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the agent; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (جعلنا) as its reason, so it stands as the mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), but the accusative [without the lām] is not permissible because the agent differs. (فيه) is attached to (يسكنوا); (النهار) is conjoined to (الليل); (مبصرا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) or a second direct object. (إن) is a particle resembling the verb; (في ذلك) is its fronted khabar; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) and (آيات) is its postponed noun; (لقوم) is an adjective, and the clause (يؤمنون) is an adjective of (قوم).
(وَيَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ فَفَزِعَ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ): (ويوم) is conjoined to «ويوم نحشر», falling under its ruling, which is the command to remember it. The clause (ينفخ) is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, its implied form being "it"; (في الصور) is attached to (ينفخ). (ففزع) is conjoined to (ينفخ); the secret of the expression with the past tense will come in the Rhetoric section. (من) is the agent of (فزع), (في السموات) is the ṣila, and (ومن في الأرض) is conjoined to (من في السموات).
(إِلَّا مَنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ وَكُلٌّ أَتَوْهُ داخِرِينَ): (إلا) is a particle of exception and (من) is the excepted; the clause (شاء الله) is the ṣila.
